title: Best parameters for FastQC on mixed read lengths?
body: I am running FastQC on a dataset that combines 75 bp and 150 bp Illumina reads. The per-base quality plots look uneven near the tail, but the samples otherwise pass. Has anyone adjusted their review criteria for mixed read lengths?
author: Mina

comments.author: Levent
comments.body: I usually split mixed read lengths before reviewing FastQC summaries. It makes the warning flags much easier to interpret.

comments.author: Aylin
comments.body: Check whether the trimming step produced the length mix. If so, MultiQC can help you compare the samples without overreacting to one warning.

comments.author: Jon
comments.body: The tail drop is common in 150 bp reads. I would focus more on adapter content and duplication than the final few bases.

title: How much memory should I reserve for BUSCO on a plant assembly?
body: My genome assembly is about 1.4 Gb and I want to run BUSCO with the embryophyta lineage. I am unsure whether to use a smaller VM first or reserve a high-memory node from the start.
author: Deniz

comments.author: Priya
comments.body: For a 1.4 Gb plant assembly I would start with at least 32 GB RAM, especially if you are running many CPUs.

comments.author: Marco
comments.body: The lineage database and temporary files matter too. Make sure your scratch disk has plenty of room.

comments.author: Selin
comments.body: If you are testing settings, run once on a small subset or with fewer threads before launching the full job.

title: SPAdes assembly failed after read correction
body: SPAdes completed the error correction stage but failed during assembly with no obvious message in the summary log. The paired-end files passed quality control. What log files should I inspect first?
author: Elif

comments.author: Ozan
comments.body: Open the main spades.log and search upward from the final error. The real cause is often a few dozen lines before the last traceback.

comments.author: Hannah
comments.body: I would also check whether the temp directory filled up. SPAdes can fail abruptly when disk space runs out.

comments.author: Burak
comments.body: If you used high k-mer values, try the default auto mode once to see whether it gets past the assembly stage.

title: Interpreting QUAST results for a fragmented metagenome assembly
body: QUAST reports a low N50 and many contigs for a metagenome assembly. The reads are from a complex soil sample, so I expected fragmentation. Which metrics are most useful in this case?
author: Nora

comments.author: Kerem
comments.body: For metagenomes, I pay more attention to total assembled length, largest contig, and misassembly warnings than N50 alone.

comments.author: Lara
comments.body: If you have a reference or binning results, run reference-based evaluation for the bins separately.

comments.author: Emre
comments.body: Fragmentation can be normal for soil. Compare against other assemblies from the same input rather than using isolate-genome expectations.

title: Liftoff gene models missing on alternate haplotigs
body: I used Liftoff to transfer annotations from a primary assembly to a haplotype-resolved assembly. Most primary chromosomes look good, but several alternate haplotigs have sparse gene coverage.
author: Cem

comments.author: Irem
comments.body: Check whether those haplotigs are highly diverged or mostly repetitive. Liftoff can miss models if the alignment identity drops.

comments.author: Sam
comments.body: You may need to relax the identity and coverage thresholds, then manually inspect the genes that move.

comments.author: Zeynep
comments.body: I would also confirm the sequence names in the target assembly. Naming mismatches can make debugging very confusing.

title: Choosing between hifiasm and Verkko for HiFi plus ONT data
body: We have PacBio HiFi reads and moderate ONT coverage for a heterozygous sample. I am comparing hifiasm and Verkko for the first assembly pass. What tradeoffs should I expect?
author: Leyla

comments.author: Arda
comments.body: hifiasm is a very strong first pass for HiFi-heavy datasets. Verkko can shine when the ONT reads help bridge repeats.

comments.author: Nina
comments.body: Run both if you can afford it, then compare contiguity, BUSCO, and k-mer completeness with Merqury.

comments.author: Can
comments.body: The best choice may depend on heterozygosity. Look carefully at duplicated BUSCOs and haplotype purging.

title: Merqury spectra-cn plot shows unexpected second peak
body: My Merqury spectra-cn plot has the expected main peak, but there is also a smaller second peak that I did not see in previous assemblies. Could this indicate retained haplotigs?
author: Sofia

comments.author: Derya
comments.body: A second peak can indicate duplicated haplotype sequence, but contamination or uneven coverage can also produce odd patterns.

comments.author: Leo
comments.body: Compare the plot with BUSCO duplication and read-depth tracks. One metric rarely tells the whole story.

comments.author: Melis
comments.body: If you have purge results, run Merqury before and after purging to see whether that peak changes.

title: MetaSPAdes output has many short contigs after host filtering
body: After host read removal, MetaSPAdes produced many short contigs and only a few above 10 kb. The sample is low biomass. Would you change the filtering or assembly settings?
author: Tuna

comments.author: Merve
comments.body: Low biomass samples often have limited microbial coverage. I would first check how many reads survived host filtering.

comments.author: Alex
comments.body: Be careful with aggressive filtering. You might be discarding microbial reads that are close to host sequence.

comments.author: Ece
comments.body: Try assembling with and without very strict quality trimming. Sometimes the stricter input fragments the graph more.

title: GenomeScope model fit looks poor for a polyploid sample
body: GenomeScope estimated genome size much lower than expected and the model fit looks poor. The organism may be polyploid and has high heterozygosity. How should I interpret the result?
author: Yasmin

comments.author: Bora
comments.body: GenomeScope can be hard to interpret for polyploids. Treat the estimate as exploratory unless the model fit is strong.

comments.author: Nadia
comments.body: Try several k values and compare the histograms. Sometimes the default k-mer size hides the real structure.

comments.author: Tolga
comments.body: External genome size evidence, like flow cytometry, is very helpful for sanity checking this case.

title: Workflow job stuck in queued state
body: A workflow job has been queued for more than an hour even though smaller jobs are completing. The input files are already uploaded. What should I check before canceling it?
author: Rana

comments.author: Kaan
comments.body: Look at the requested VM size and partition. Large memory requests may wait while smaller jobs continue to run.

comments.author: Julia
comments.body: Check whether the job is waiting for a file staging step. Uploaded does not always mean copied into the execution workspace.

comments.author: Sarp
comments.body: If it is reproducible, capture the job id and queue status before canceling so the admin can inspect it.

title: Recommended naming convention for pipeline outputs
body: Our group is building reusable pipelines and wants output names that are clear across projects. Do people prefer sample-first names, tool-first names, or nested folders by tool?
author: Ipek

comments.author: Noah
comments.body: I prefer sample-first filenames inside tool-specific folders. It keeps comparisons easy without huge filenames.

comments.author: Asli
comments.body: Include the major parameter set only when it changes the interpretation, otherwise names become too long.

comments.author: Mehmet
comments.body: A small README or manifest in each run folder saves a lot of confusion later.

title: FastQC adapter warning after trimming
body: FastQC still reports adapter content after I trimmed with a standard adapter list. The warning is low but appears in multiple samples. Should I re-trim with custom adapters?
author: Ari

comments.author: Defne
comments.body: Inspect the overrepresented sequences. If they match a library-specific adapter, custom trimming is worth it.

comments.author: Mateo
comments.body: A tiny residual signal may not matter, especially if the reads map well and downstream metrics are stable.

comments.author: Ekin
comments.body: Run MultiQC across the batch. A pattern across samples often points to library prep rather than a one-off issue.

title: Can I reuse a Meryl database across assemblies?
body: I built a Meryl database from the raw reads for one assembly evaluation. Can I reuse the same database for later assemblies from the same sample, or should I rebuild it each time?
author: Berk

comments.author: Ela
comments.body: You can reuse the read k-mer database for assemblies from the same read set and k value.

comments.author: Victor
comments.body: Document the k value and input read files carefully. Reuse gets risky when those details are unclear.

comments.author: Gunes
comments.body: If reads were filtered or corrected differently, rebuild so the comparison remains honest.

title: Handling large reference files in shared storage
body: Several workflows use the same large reference genome and annotation files. Uploading them into every project wastes storage. What is the cleanest way to manage shared references?
author: Seda

comments.author: Omer
comments.body: A shared read-only references folder works well if permissions are handled carefully.

comments.author: Grace
comments.body: Version the reference directory names. Even small annotation updates can change downstream results.

comments.author: Alp
comments.body: Store checksums next to the files so users can verify they are pointing to the expected version.

title: What should go into a reproducible run note?
body: I want every completed analysis to have a short note that makes it reproducible later. Beyond tool versions and input files, what else should be captured?
author: Maya

comments.author: Eren
comments.body: Record parameters, reference versions, container image tags, and the exact workflow revision.

comments.author: Clara
comments.body: Add a short reason for non-default settings. Future you will appreciate knowing why a value changed.

comments.author: Fatma
comments.body: I also include resource settings and runtime. They help when planning the next run.
